intuition.title: Water-to-surfactant ratio and particle size
intuition.text: The source compares unannealed w = 3 and w = 5 powders and reports mean TEM sizes of4.5 and7.4nm, respectively. It attributes the larger size to greater water/AOT ratio. Exact w = 3 precursor and water charges are missing, so the result is not converted into a complete alternative charge recipe.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures3–4 and size discussion

intuition.title: Small TEM counts limit the conclusion
intuition.text: Agglomeration prevents an accurate particle-size distribution. The reported means use21particles forw = 3 and28forw = 5, with estimated mean-size uncertainty strictly<10%. This is not a polydispersity value or normal-distribution standard deviation.

intuition.title: Thermoelectric motivation remains future work
intuition.text: The introduction discusses quantum-confinement predictions and earlier thermoelectric systems. The present paper supplies synthesis, elemental analysis, diffraction and microscopy; measuring quantum-confinement effects on thermoelectric properties is left to future work. No current Seebeck coefficient, conductivity or thermoelectric figure of merit is assigned.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
